demand_supply.scope: World nitrogen, annualized calendar-year approximation; own scenario model, not a project-by-project census
demand_supply.units: million metric tonnes of contained nitrogen unless stated
demand_supply.limitations: IFA 2024 capability 166.6 and forecast 2026-30 increase 17 anchor an explicitly assumed 174 baseline in 2026. The 40 industrial-use baseline is an analyst assumption with a 35-45 uncertainty range. Crop-year fertilizer use is mapped to calendar years approximately. Capability already includes normal achievable utilization; no second utilization or yield haircut is applied. Temporary outages and permanent economic closures are separate deductions. Announced additions are not all financed, operating or interchangeable. No global inventory series or complete project qualification census was verified.
demand_supply.formula: Crop activity proxy = 2965 million tonnes 2026 cereal utilization * (1+activity_growth)^(year-2026). Desired fertilizer N = activity * (118.9/2965) * intensity_factor. Financially supported demand = desired demand * affordability_factor. Available fertilizer N = productive capability - temporary/geographic unavailability - economic closures - industrial N use. Fulfilled demand = min(supported demand, available fertilizer N). The cereal proxy holds the noncereal crop mix proportionate; it is not a claim that all fertilizer is used on cereals.

reverse_operating_price.unit: fraction of base core product selling prices
reverse_operating_price.method: Raise affected revenue by uplift, add the same amount to EBIT, and hold 2026-35 base costs, CHS claims, working capital and capex fixed. Solve fair value = current price. For CF the 2036-40 reinvestment transition responds mechanically to changed NOPAT; GSL keeps the same finite residual. This is one price-justifying combination, not consensus.

demand_supply.scope: Sub-10000 TEU containership segment normalized to 1000 beginning productive TEU; 2026 is September run rate, later years annual averages
demand_supply.units: TEU-days per standardized 1000 starting TEU; cargo in representative annual TEU movements, not absolute world cargo
demand_supply.limitations: The absolute sub-10000 TEU fleet and individual financing/yard-status census were not verified. This is a transparent normalized supply diagnostic, not a complete global capacity forecast. The 24.7% orderbook-to-fleet anchor is an external MSI estimate reproduced in a company presentation; not an independent second source. Other cohorts can cascade into or substitute for parts of this segment. Deliveries after 2030 include additional orders induced by high profits, assumed rather than announced; the upside has faster investment response from 2031. Required demand above usable capacity is unmet desired cargo work, not realized ship revenue.
demand_supply.formula: Installed closing TEU = opening TEU + delivered additions - retirements. Average productive TEU = opening TEU + 0.5*(additions-retirements). Usable supply = average productive TEU * 365 * technical availability. Required TEU-days = 10000 starting representative annual cargo TEU * cumulative cargo growth * 35.04 baseline days per move * voyage/cycle factor. Baseline cycle calibrates starting demand to 350400 TEU-days. No cargo revenue is counted again as shipowner revenue. Technical availability and cycle-time losses are separate; ordinary utilization is an output, not an extra deduction.

reverse_operating_price.method: Raise affected revenue by uplift, add the same amount to EBIT, and hold 2026-35 base costs, CHS claims, working capital and capex fixed. Solve fair value = current price. For CF the 2036-40 reinvestment transition responds mechanically to changed NOPAT; GSL keeps the same finite residual. This is one price-justifying combination, not consensus.
